Preprint:
	arxiv.org/1202.4355
	Low Degree Places on the Modular Curve X1(N)
	(2012 version: had N = 29, 31, and the degree 6 point for N = 37)
	(2013 version: added a table for N <= 60)

We search for places v for which we do not have a function of degree deg(v).
For example, X1(25) has functions of degrees 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12,...
so we search for places of degrees 1,2,3,4, 6,7.  Although the degrees 6,7
are higher than the gonality, these places are nevertheless of interest
since X1(25) has only finitely many places of those degrees.

Notation: For each place v on X1(N) that we found, listed are:

	(1) N = 
	(2) degv = [Q(v):Q]
	(3) degj = [Q(j):Q]   (this is only listed if it differs from degv)
	(4) j =               (this is only listed if j in Q)
	(5) [eqx, eqxy]       An equation in x, and an equation in x,y.

Let (x0,y0) be a solution of eqx, eqxy.  Then let:

	r := (x0^2*y0-x0*y0+y0-1)/(x0^2*y0-x0)
        s := (x0*y0-y0+1)/(x0*y0)
        b := r*s*(r-1)
        c := s*(r-1)
	E := Y^2 + (1-c)*X*Y - b*Y = X^3 - b*X^2
	P := The point (0,0) on E.

Then P is a point on E of order N.


Only one member from each diamond-orbit is listed.   We used a probabilistic
search (for N > 42 it is likely that some diamond-orbits are missing).  The
point for N = 21 was already found by Najman in arxiv.org/1211.2188.


                                              Mark van Hoeij, Aug 2013.
